task.instructions:
Using matplotlib, create a vertical bar chart from the records below. Each record lists year, status, channel, impressions, and clicks.

2025, final, Search, 100, 30
2025, final, Search, 900, 60
2025, final, Social, 200, 20
2025, final, Social, 800, 10
2025, final, Email, 100, 30
2025, final, Email, 900, 90
2024, final, Search, 1000, 400
2024, final, Social, 1000, 600
2024, final, Email, 1000, 200
2025, draft, Search, 1000, 500
2025, draft, Social, 1000, 700
2025, draft, Email, 1000, 100

Use only records from 2025 with status final. For each channel, calculate the click-through rate as 100 times total clicks divided by total impressions across the retained records. Do not average the individual records' click-through rates. Plot the channels from highest to lowest rate, with one blue bar per channel. Label each bar with its rate to one decimal place followed by a percent sign. Use the title 'Final campaign click-through rates (2025)', the x-axis label 'Channel', and the y-axis label 'Click-through rate (%)'. Set the y-axis limits to 0 and 15. Use a 6 by 4 inch figure at 150 DPI. Keep all text fully visible and readable, and save the chart as figure.png.

function.arguments:
{"command": "cat <<'EOF' > generate_chart.py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Data from the records (year, status, channel, impressions, clicks)
records = [
    (2025, 'final', 'Search', 100, 30),
    (2025, 'final', 'Search', 900, 60),
    (2025, 'final', 'Social', 200, 20),
    (2025, 'final', 'Social', 800, 10),
    (2025, 'final', 'Email', 100, 30),
    (2025, 'final', 'Email', 900, 90),
    (2024, 'final', 'Search', 1000, 400),
    (2024, 'final', 'Social', 1000, 600),
    (2024, 'final', 'Email', 1000, 200),
    (2025, 'draft', 'Search', 1000, 500),
    (2025, 'draft', 'Social', 1000, 700),
    (2025, 'draft', 'Email', 1000, 100),
]

# Filter records: only 2025 with status "final"
filtered_records = [r for r in records if r[0] == 2025 and r[1] == 'final']

# Calculate total impressions and clicks per channel
channel_data = {}
for year, status, channel, impressions, clicks in filtered_records:
    if channel not in channel_data:
        channel_data[channel] = {'impressions': 0, 'clicks': 0}
    channel_data[channel]['impressions'] += impressions
    channel_data[channel]['clicks'] += clicks

# Calculate CTR for each channel
channel_ctr = {}
for channel, data in channel_data.items():
    ctr = 100 * data['clicks'] / data['impressions']
    channel_ctr[channel] = ctr

# Sort channels from highest to lowest CTR
sorted_channels = sorted(channel_ctr.keys(), key=lambda x: channel_ctr[x], reverse=True)
sorted_ctrs = [channel_ctr[channel] for channel in sorted_channels]

# Create the bar chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4), dpi=150)

bars = ax.bar(sorted_channels, sorted_ctrs, color='blue')

# Label each bar with its rate
for bar, ctr in zip(bars, sorted_ctrs):
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2., height,
            f'{ctr:.1f}%',
            ha='center', va='bottom')

# Set title and labels
ax.set_title('Final campaign click-through rates (2025)')
ax.set_xlabel('Channel')
ax.set_ylabel('Click-through rate (%)')

# Set y-axis limits
ax.set_ylim(0, 15)

# Save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('figure.png', dpi=150)

print("Chart saved as figure.png")
print(f"Channels sorted by CTR (highest to lowest):")
for channel, ctr in zip(sorted_channels, sorted_ctrs):
    print(f"  {channel}: {ctr:.1f}%")
EOF
"}
